===== SENDMESSAGE to: aa83b18c673632e35 | Design amendment: twin-form windowed body | ts - =====
DESIGN AMENDMENT — I407-DESIGN.md layers 4-6 have changed; re-read the file. The amendment, and why:

PROBLEM with the original layer 5 (replace the m=1 bodies with gathered windowed ones): at 1 resident page a W=8 window sweeps 8 pages of KV — 7 of them padded-by-own-last-page and masked. The copy still READS them: ~7 extra pages × ~40 MB/page(all layers) of pool reads + scratch writes + fold reads ≈ +9-14 ms on a ~185 ms step = +5-7% ITL at shallow context. That is the canonical short-ctx regime; it must not move.

AMENDED DESIGN — twin-form, one new body:
1. The m=1 family KEEPS every existing plain per-rung body, bit-identical, still selected exactly as today when n_fold_pages < W. Do not touch their emission.
2. ADD one windowed twin per m=1 bucket: gathered, W-page sweep, selected at step time iff n_fold_pages >= W (a full window exists). The selection branch lives where the executor picks the rung body today (superdsc_exec) — the twin wins over the plain bodies only on that predicate.
3. The windowed twin is RUNG-INDEPENDENT — exactly one twin, not one per rung: its sweep is W × PAGE_SLOTS including a FULL tail page, and the tail is cut by the host-staged MASK, never by rung active_cap. This is how the batched gathered body already cuts per-request tails (one body serves rows at different depths, so the mask must do it) — verify that mechanism in the batched staging (spyre_exec.rs ~:1183-1250) and reuse it for the solo twin. The wasted tail columns (≤255 slots of one page) cost ~0.5 ms/step — negligible against the relaunch savings.
4. Layer 6 updates: KvShifts.pages_per_pass — plain bodies stamp 1, the twin stamps W; fold_plan::reps = ceil(n_fold_pages / W) for the twin only; the host staging stages the 1-row W-page index table + W-page mask blocks per pass, where the mask kills BOTH the final partial window's surplus pages AND the last live page's tail.

Layers 1-3 (const row + Window<W> witness, PageScratch W, page_gather_index_table W) are unchanged. The validation section's new-unit-tests item changes accordingly: the twin-selection predicate (n_fold_pages >= W) and the twin's mask-both-roles staging deserve tests; reps=ceil and the index padding tests stand.

Everything else in your original instructions stands (scope walls, gates, no commits, report format). If you already built parts of layer 5 in the replace-shape, rework them to the twin-shape — the windowed body construction itself should carry over.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: aa599714aee075771 | fused-rung panic is on main: fix it properly, own PR | ts - =====
I verified the panic on upstream/main 6a211686b: superdsc_exec.rs:1028 builds `body_rungs_fused` with `.filter(|fp| !fp.is_none())`, and `select_body_paged` (:2212) returns `RungFused(i)` regardless. It's a main bug from #299, so rebasing won't fix it. And it's worse than the empty case: the filter COLLAPSES class indices, so if class 0 sits out and class 1 has a twin, `list(c=0)` silently runs class 1's ops. Fix it properly, as its own PR cut from upstream/main (fix(spyre): …), not a bake-tree hack:
1. Keep the class position: store per class an `Option<Ops>` (or a typed per-class twin), so a class index can't address another class's body. Make the misalignment unrepresentable, per the compile-time-guard rule.
2. Select `RungFused(i)` only when every live class of that rung has a twin; otherwise fall through to `select_body`.
3. Write a test that a rung with all classes sitting out selects the split body, and one where class 0 sits out and class 1 doesn't never runs class 1's ops for class 0.
Then bake 2b fp16 from 6a211686b + this fix + 8dbe9dee7/0fe2ec2c1 (bake tree only) on nickm 0-47, and run the card checks (id ≥8192 share, 10k NLL vs a main binary that has this fix but not the scalarmul fix, --max-model-len 69632). I'm telling #299's author.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: flex-rs | fused quantize is prime; check the UNSEEDED reduce first | ts - =====
Agreed, the fused per-token quantize fits every constraint. Inside it, check the UNSEEDED reduce first. An abs-max reduce with no seed starts from whatever sits in its accumulator, so stale LX or HBM contents (another op's leftovers) join the max. The result is a wrong per-token scale on every fp8 matmul, fluent-and-wrong, and different per tree because the memory history differs. That matches "Fr4" vs "France" and the 26b fp8 garbage too. Also check the padded tail: a reduce over a stick-padded K that reads the pad as data. The good pole's chain seeded its amax explicitly (absx/amax host-materialized). If the fused op's seed or init is missing, that's the bug, and the fix is a seed plus a build-time refusal of an unseeded max-reduce. The decode worker's 2b fp8 bake on 6a211686b + both fixes + #563 is running on nickm now; I'll forward the reply the moment it lands.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: a20be7fe799f7f5d6 | deeptools source shows the mul's fast path conditions | ts - =====
The user pointed us at the deeptools source in ~/git/deeptools; use it for the mulsilu question. What I found in dvs/setupVariables/add_mul_sub_fwd.cpp (the setup behind MUL → add_mul_sub_fwd.smc):
- The binary op takes a FAST path only when `fuseLoops` is set (lines ~116–160): both inputs share the same scale_ AND the same layoutDimOrder_ as the output, and either Dloops aren't needed or all three operands share one LX-optimized state (`lxOptMap[labeledDs_A]["LU"] == lxOptMap[labeledDs_B]["LU"] == lxOptMap[labeledDs_output]["SU"]`). With fuseLoops, the load/store offsets collapse to a flat 128·ncl stride (one fused loop). Otherwise it walks the general per-dim loop nest (the `else` arm at ~:280: strides per inner dim), which is the slow form.
- The unary silu (tanh_rsqrt_reciprocal_exp_sigmoid_fwd.cpp, doFastSilu) has no such condition, so it always streams.
So check mulsilu_o461's descriptor for exactly those three things:
(1) do tmp (silu's output) and up have IDENTICAL layoutDimOrder_ and scale_ as the mul's output?
(2) do the three operands agree on LX-optimized state? E.g. if silu leaves tmp LX-resident (LU) but up comes from HBM, the condition fails and it falls back to the loop nest.
(3) Dloops_needed.
If one differs, emitting the mul so its operands agree (same layout, same LX state) should give the fused-loop rate, roughly silu's per byte. Report which condition fails; the source is the authority (POD C++ / deeptools source > our docs).

CONTRADICTIONS. Fix these first, since they change our own ledger.

1. The #500 TODO 4 barrier claim is WRONG for compute CBs.

   - So barrier_launches (superdsc_exec.rs:2701) counts host fence calls, not device barriers. Device ordering today is ring FIFO plus cmpt.sync=1 (always set: control_block_wire.rs:844, pod :294).
   - Correct #500 TODO 4 and the #549 ledger: the "42 barrier launches / ≤10 µs settles" are not device barriers.

2. telemetry.rs:2-3 claims LatencyBreakdown, Histogram and HistTimer ports; their sections (:265-273) are empty (R). Fix the doc or port them.
3. telemetry.rs says AIUPTI lives in libaiupti. On the pod it's in flex's own src/telemetry/aiupti_profiler.cpp (R).
4. hazards.rs's doc says the vendor tracker isn't shipped. It is (pod src/runtime_stream/scheduler/hazard_tracker.cpp), and it differs:
   - compute footprint is READS only;
   - Fill is untracked;
   - it keeps last-writer/reader history, not an outstanding set;
   - edges are EventWait/EventSignal ops on scheduler queues;
   - it has a RAS Deadlock detector;
   - it's off unless SPYRE_HAZARD_TRACKER=1.
   Ours is conservative (read+write on everything). Document the divergence; don't copy the reads-only hole.
5. 1p5/UMI: pod flex's UmiRuntimeScheduler/UmiDeviceInterface are THROWING STUBS (umi_runtime_scheduler.cpp:56, :77; device_1p5_memory_addressing.hpp:69, :81) (R). For Spyre II the only reference is senlib 1.5 (/opt/ibm/spyre/senlib/include).

DESIGN ANSWERS FOR #603
- Q1: no next-CB or loop pointer. A CB is six sections, CTRL@0 R5@8 DMI@16 DMO@32 CMPT@48 XLAT@64 (control_block_sbf.hpp:36-41); the ring is the chain. "memcpy+patch+one doorbell" is exactly the vendor batch branch QueueControlBlocksSBF(&GetCB(0), N) (response_worker.cpp:1373). The vendor DOES build once and resubmit: timestamp_calibrator.cpp:304 builds calibration_cbs_ once, and :773 resubmits a ControlBlockChunk every round. PrepareCbs re-tags whatever it's handed (response_worker.cpp:888) (R).
- Q2a, tags: unique while in flight. The constraint is flex's 16-bit pending_requests_[tag & 0xFFFF] map, a 32768-tag pool from 1 (runtime_config.cpp:112, response_worker.cpp:456-470) (R). If we own the tag space, partition it: tag = base(step mod D) + i, a compile-time constant plus one affine term (I).
- Q2b, RBs: CANNOT be suppressed. Every CB yields an RB that must be harvested and credited back via FreeResponses (response_worker.cpp:1250-1262). The same holds on 1.5 (256-B request+response slots, msh_base.hpp) (R). So: one grouped callback per step, as your note says.
- Q3, depth: the ring is 32768 on the pod (senlib_config_controls_1p0.json:21), the gate is in_flight+new ≤ capacity, and tags cap at 32768 (Precheck MaxCbsExceeded, response_worker.cpp:613-631). At 162 CBs/step that's ~200 steps of headroom. The real k-limit is per-step HOST buffers (logits, preamble) (I).
- Q4, 1.5: MessageStream IS resubmittable after completion (message_stream.hpp:53-63; msh_deferred_builder.hpp:86 handles "second finalize").
  - submitBlocking(strm, k) with burst k, submitNonBlocking returns a future, ≤16 AppIDs, credit flow via MaxCredit (message_interface.hpp:55, :134, :147, :183).
  - Setters THROW while in flight, so double-buffer D streams or copyAppend/copySpliceAfter a template.
  - finalize() recomputes guards on every submit (message_stream.hpp:724): unavoidable per-message host work.
  - Handles are named with O(1) find(name), so patch points come by name.
  - No user tag setter (GetRspSqn), so the tag patch likely disappears on 1.5.
  - Addressing via MshActivate once per bucket could leave compute messages carrying only a program DVA and core mask (I).
  So L1's image+patch design maps onto 1.5. Keep the patch-table abstraction target-ABI-neutral (a const table per CLAUDE.md), so 1.5 is a new emitter, not a rewrite.

- G1, CB template/Specialize lifecycle (control_block_stream.hpp:24, 271-307, 340, 398-464). - G3, CreateNullCb / launchNullOperation / submitNullOp (control_block_stream.hpp:257, runtime_stream.hpp:328, pf_runtime_scheduler.cpp:501). A null CB with barrier=1 is the vendor's cheapest device fence, and could be the one "end of step" RB.

Cause: that shape is stick-major rank-2, so the law now splits it out:32 (one stick × 31 rows per core). That gives a start delta of rows·stk·2 = 3968, where torch-spyre's row split gives 128. Your gate list missed this because these are scratchy-target-spyre integration tests. They're in the splice job, which you didn't run verbatim, and #615's author hit the same gap. 1. These tests make TWO claims. Keep both, at full strength.
   (a) TORCH-SPYRE PARITY: given torch-spyre's division, our emission machinery produces torch-spyre's bytes. Keep pointwise_31x2048_matches_torchspyre exactly as is, but have it state RowsFirst explicitly (the division torch-spyre uses for this shape). The law deliberately chooses a different division, measured faster on card; that division doesn't change the parity claim about the machinery. If the door has no way to take an explicit division, add one; the gathered-row leg already passes RowsFirst.
   (b) SINGLE-SOURCE LAYOUT: the start delta and coordInfo derive from the one SpyreTensorLayout. Keep these tests on the SHIPPED division (the law), and derive the expected values from the layout along the split axis. Under out:32 the expected delta is the layout's feat-group stride (rows·stk·2 = 3968), and elem_arr_1 is device_size[0] / out_split. Compute both from `stl`, never hard-code them. Keep the "not the flat r*cols hack" negative assertion (4096), since that's still the bug these tests exist to catch.
2. Add one test that pins, for this exact torch-spyre shape, that the shipped law division is out:32 and that it differs from torch-spyre's, with a comment saying why (the measured (e) cells).
3. Grep crates/targets/spyre/tests and ktir-superdsc/tests for every other test that pins a pointwise per-core start, coordInfo or wk-slice on a stick-major rank-2 shape, and treat each the same way.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/63668.sock | PR3: price composite argmax (max+eq+iota) first | ts - =====
Thorough read. argmax.ddl being unreachable through the selection table is decisive, and it's better to learn that from source than from a wrong-kernel bug. My ruling:

NOT (i) as the plan. Host argmax plus a device gather leaves the host round trip in place, and removing it is the whole point of loop closure (and what makes k>1 possible). I also doubt (i) saves ~1 ms. It replaces one per-step H2D (the 8 KB embedding row) with another (a 4 B index), and both are one DMA CB with the same fixed cost. Show me which phase of the 1.5 ms (i) actually removes before anyone builds it.

Price option (iv) instead: a COMPOSITE argmax from table-reachable, multi-core primitives, with first-max by construction and no dependence on topk's ambiguous tie-break.
1. m = max-reduce over vocab. summeanmaxexx2 has max, and it splits across cores; check the table entry.
2. mask = (logits == m), a broadcast eq comparison from broadcast_ops' comparisons.
3. w = mask · (V − iota), with a resident fp32 constant iota, so the first maximal index gets the largest weight.
4. j = max-reduce(w) in fp32 (summeanmaxexx2_fp32), then idx = V − j, then Fp32ToInt32. The gather follows, using the MoE router's chain as the template.
Ties resolve to the smallest index by arithmetic, the same first-max as #631. Price it cardless: selection-table entries for every op, dxp rc=0 on the group, and perfEst per op. Two questions to answer along the way:
- Your ~170 µs for dl16tofp32 at vocab width looks wrong. 49152 × 2 B is ~98 KB, which is ~2 µs at copy rates across 32 cores. What geometry gives 170 µs (one core? stick padding)? If (iv) does the compare in fp16 and converts only the {0,1} mask, does the cost move?
- Can the lm_head matmul emit fp32 directly? That would remove the convert altogether.

If (iv) prices well under the 1.5 ms it removes, it's PR3a (k=1), and PR3b (k>1) follows on top of it. If it doesn't, then (ii), with your topk tie probe first.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/4805.sock | rinv pin overflow = bump allocator; fix direction | ts - =====
I read main's code, and your numbers already explain the overflow, so the producer grep can drop in priority.
- **What the pin is.** The only caller of `synth_lx` on main is the rmsnorm `rinv` at rmsnorm.rs:95: `[rows, 64]` fp16 = rows × 128 B. 65,536 B means rows = 512, the 512-row prompt chunk.
- **Why it overflows.** `LxAlloc` bumps per tensor and never reuses a pin (placement.rs:385, deliberately "even where lifetimes would allow sharing"). So every rmsnorm in one bundle stacks another 64 KiB. (1,589,248 − 131,072) / 65,536 ≈ 22 earlier pins, so this bundle has about 23 norms. That's gemma's per-layer norm count times the layers grouped into the bundle at GROUP_SIZE=512.
- **It isn't a #632 regression.** Before #632 the ceiling was 2 MiB. Pins between 1,625,344 and 2 MiB sat inside dxp's frontend LX allocations: landings measured at 1.62–1.84 MiB per the LX_PIN_BASE doc. So pre-#632 bakes of this fixture had a latent on-card overlap. #632 turned it into a build failure, which is what it was for. Say exactly this in the report, and if the old pre-#632 bake ran on card, check whether it matched the emulator.
- **Fix direction** for the owner, i.e. you, unless you hand it back. Option (a): colour LX pins by lifetime, the way intermediate slots already are. rinv dies at its xn consumer, so one 64 KiB slot serves every norm. The pipeline already computes lifetimes at expansion, so this isn't emission-order luck. Option (b): rinv core-local, `rows/32 × 128` B = 2 KiB per core. That needs the producer's division to match the reader's, and today the producer replicates. (a) is the general fix.
- **Before anything else:** count the rmsnorms per bundle in the real 26b and 12b at main. If any bundle is within 2 pins of the ceiling, say so. Their bake passing today doesn't mean they have headroom.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/4805.sock | witness budget must subtract the rinv slot | ts - =====
The design shape works if one thing holds: the rinv slot sits above the chunk's high-water mark, and that slot must also be inside the witness's budget. If it isn't, the witness admits a chunk that fits alone but not together with the slot. The witness's budget should be the window minus that bundle's op-local slots, and the reservation is a compile-time function of the bundle: one class at rows = the bundle's mq, footprint rows×128. Granite-8b's 40-page chunk works out to 128 KiB base + 1,280 KiB + 64 KiB rinv at mq=512 = 1,507,328, under 1,625,344, so it fits today. But the witness has to compute that, not assume it. The post-emission walk that panics on any same-slot interleave is the right backstop. The op-name detector fix (attn_cgkt_/attn_cgv_/attn_nc*) is the same lesson as "a verdict over nothing must fail": give the scan script a guard so that 0 detected chunk ops on a model with chunk forms fails the scan.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/4805.sock | LX colouring design approved; per-group slot + walk | ts - =====
The design is approved, with these rulings on the three questions.

**(1) Programs.** A launch group's `programs` run IN ORDER (bundle/src/lib.rs `LaunchGroup::programs`: "the programs this launch runs, IN ORDER"). A bundle's `groups` are its launches in launch order on one stream, so nothing in a bundle runs concurrently. Even so, scope it at the narrowest level that still collapses the stack: one shared slot per launch GROUP (a group is one dxp compile, so one LX allocation domain). Make the walk run per group from day one, over that group's programs in order. dxp only sees one group at a time, so sharing across groups buys nothing.

**(2) The 16 KiB.** Find it first. A 16 KiB pin at mq=512 means 32 B per row, too small for rinv. Look for a second `synth_lx_core_local` caller outside attn.rs, or anything the MoE path pins. Name it before the bake set runs. If it's a chunk pin, that bundle becomes your real-model norm+chunk witness.

**(3) Emit order.** Don't assume it. The walk's first run on the full bake set is the measurement. If it fails anywhere at land time, that is a finding: report which class interleaves and where, and don't widen the walk to make it pass.

One more requirement: the computed witness budget must come from the same function the allocator's final assert uses. Put it in one place, so the two can't drift.

Go code it on a fresh branch off main. 26b at 74% free with no chunk forms is good headroom news.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: a95ebfa70f95cf21a | #651: descriptor digest OK; deterministic + asserting early-out | ts - =====
The descriptor digest is the right fix: it covers every input by construction, including the emitter's code version. Two constraints:
1. **Keep it cheap and deterministic.** The digest has to hash the rendered descriptor bytes in a stable order. Use the same serialization the dump writes and dxp reads, not a Debug print or a HashMap iteration order. Prove determinism: two builds of one tree must give identical fps, so check 2b fp16 twice at one tree.
2. **The early-out stays on a pre-lowering key, but it must ASSERT.** On a pre-key hit, compute the new bundle's digest too and panic if it differs from the stored one. That keeps the early-out safe without paying the lowering cost on every hit.
Your PlanKey work may become redundant once the digest covers everything. Keep whichever is simpler, and say in the body why. Your nickm cargo still stops at 03:00Z: finish the 8b and gemma pairs for the current form first, then do the digest change cardless. Its bakes run after the sweep.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/70581.sock | #670: gap needs a concurrent writer; check mask fill | ts - =====
Accepted: the kzero/kreps quartet is co-lead with fq_mm. Two sharpenings for check 2.
(1) A coverage gap is a MECHANISM, not a SOURCE. The B leg (fixed predecessor, still scatters) acquitted cross-process residue. So unwritten seg1 tail rows would hold the same bytes run to run, UNLESS something inside the same process writes them nondeterministically. For each tail byte range a gap leaves unwritten, list every op in the same launch group (and the prior group) that also writes those seg1 bytes, with its core. A concurrent writer on another core is the race. That joins your intra-group-ordering suspect to the gap, and it's what the fix must refuse at bake time.
(2) Garbage finite K only leaks past the mask if the mask isn't a true −inf. Check the mask's fill value and how it's applied (additive constant vs select). An additive −65504 is beaten by a q·k that overflows to +inf or exceeds 65504 on garbage rows, while a −inf or select mask is immune to finite garbage. NaN rows poison every lane, which would give consistent garbage, not subtle divergence. Report the fill value and op with file:line. If it's a select or −inf, the quartet can only matter through V (0·NaN), so also say whether kreps copies V tail rows from unwritten scratch.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/70581.sock | #670: keep finite mask; fix = write-coverage refusal | ts - =====
Mask fact verified on upstream/main: spyre_forward.rs:214 and :1543, mask_neg = −(f16::MAX/2), additive. Ruling: NO separate mask issue, and NO mask change folded into #670's fix.
- The finite fill is deliberate. The comment at :1540-1542 says it's chosen so exp(score + mask) underflows and "stays finite". A true −inf makes a fully masked row's softmax max −inf, so x − max = NaN. Every pad row of a padded chunk is that case. Swapping the fill trades one hazard for a certain one.
- A select mask would be a kernel change with its own bake and parity cost, unjustified while the mask holds for every K the model can produce: real |q·k·scale| sits orders of magnitude under 32752, and stale K in a reused page is real K.
- The defect is unwritten bytes reaching the pool. That's what the fix targets, and what the bake must refuse: every byte a pool-page copy (kreps) reads must be written by some op earlier in program order, or zeroed. If that predicate holds, the mask's margin is never tested by garbage.
Record the mask fact and this reasoning in #670 as one paragraph, so nobody re-proposes −inf. Continue check 2: K and V tail-row coverage at rung 80 by kzero, and the concurrent-writer list.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/70581.sock | #565 lead: dl16tofp32 stagger may permute expert idx | ts - =====
Possible #565 lead from flex-rs's PR3a root cause. The dl16tofp32 upcast writes fp32 in a STAGGERED element arrangement: each fp16 stick spans a pair of fp32 sticks, and within each 64-element window logical L=8k+w lands at physical lane 4k+w (w<4) or 4k+(w−4)+32 (w≥4). See torch-spyre ops/eager.py:743-758 and _inductor/customops.py:1266-1324. Any lane-aligned consumer that assumes a flat layout misaligns by that permutation. flex-rs flagged that the MoE expert-gather index chain (dl16tofp32 → fp32toint32, mb-sticked) consumes an upcast result lane-aligned. If the router's expert indices are permuted, the combine picks wrong experts' outputs, which fits a 0.48-0.59 correlation. flex-rs is reading it cardlessly now and will copy you. Your shape4 localization worker should test this directly: compare the router idx tensor card vs emu FIRST.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: spyre-run-helper | Warm-build rules + the 5 traps that go cold | ts - =====
WARM BUILDS: a hard rule, and the traps that have silently made "warm" builds cold today. A cold build costs 10-25 min; a warm one ~2-3 min.
1. Reuse a WARM target dir: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/work/sweep/target on nickm, or a cp -a of it. Never a fresh target dir per build.
2. Set SCRATCHY_SUPERDSC_CACHE explicitly to a cp -a copy of THAT pod's own dxp store. Without it the store falls back to a per-profile dir and everything recompiles.
   - nickm: /work/g674-cache
   - nickm2: /work/.superdsc-cache
   - nickm4: /work/n4-main-store
   Stores DON'T transfer between pods (the identity hashes the pod's dxp_standalone; a foreign store gets wiped on open).
3. Build in the SAME env the store was made in: a `bash -l` login shell. A different env hashes to a different identity and WIPES the copied store.
4. git archive + `tar -x -m` gives fresh mtimes. Without -m, cargo can reuse another tree's rlibs and hand you a STALE binary. After every build, check the worker crate compiled from YOUR tree's path (grep `Compiling scratchy-serving-worker` in the log), and that two different shas give different md5s.
5. On each BAKE line, report wall, store entries before/after, and new dxp compiles. Many new compiles on a warm build means something went cold: stop and tell me.
6. The ONLY cold build is a 2b fp8 bake-time law pair (fresh store, by request). Never for a timing run.
Never background a pod build from the Mac; fire it detached ON the pod (setsid nohup).

===== SENDMESSAGE to: spyre-perf-helper | Before R1: why not gather V over a whole-pool row view? | ts - =====
HOLD the re-layout. R1 puts a two-region pool, a split page stride and per-op V geometry into decode's cache write and prefill's attention. That's a big blast radius for PR-C, which is a read-only decode kernel. Before I rule, answer this, because your first survey already pointed at it:

(E) NO RE-LAYOUT. State the twin's V operand as a view over the WHOLE pool (or the launch's kv-shifted window) as rows of hd elements: [pool_bytes / (hd·2), hd]. Every V row (page, layer, kvh, slot) is a contiguous [1, hd] row at a fixed row index in that view (v_write_off already proves contiguity, and plane_stride/layer_stride are multiples of a stick block, so V-row starts are row-aligned). v_ids carry the absolute row index: the interleave's Knat/Kᵀ rows simply never appear among the ids. One value tensor, one index, one scale, so the one-gather-pair law holds, and nothing else in the pool, launch ABI or writers changes.

Check, with file:line or the arithmetic:
(1) Is the V-row start always a multiple of hd·2 bytes from the view base, at both hd=64 and hd=128?
(2) The i32 id range: the 2b c8 pool is 9.6 GiB / 128 B ≈ 80 M rows, under 2³¹. And 8b?
(3) Relative to the kv-shifted base, are ids layer-independent, so v_ids is staged once per step and not per layer?
(4) Does anything in the gather descriptor or dxp require the value tensor to be "dense content", vs any row array? The case rows already bake with a 128 B row skip.
If (E) holds, the re-layout and R1 aren't needed. If it fails, tell me exactly which check fails, and then we decide on R1.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: flex-rs | USER: fix the aliasing by TYPE, not a patched offset | ts - =====
USER DIRECTIVE, verbatim: "if matmuls are reading past end of things, then that is a sign you aren't coding this properly. we are a procmacro compiler. everything is a constant. this stuff cannot compile. use the rust type system. imperative".

So don't fix matmul_o1171 by correcting the offset arithmetic. Fix it by making the mismatch unwritable. Today assemble_matmul takes an operand NAME and a raw offset (a_off/w_off/o_off → into_raw_elems()) from two different authorities, and the bounds check only fires deep in emission (assemble.rs:337).
Required shape:
- A typed `Window` (placement id + start + extent, in ONE unit type) constructible ONLY through the placement: e.g. `placement.window(start, extent) -> Result<Window, _>`, checked at construction.
- `matmul_opspec_off` and every matmul operand take `Window`, never (name, raw offset). The raw-offset parameters are deleted.
- So an out-of-bounds window fails where its offset is COMPUTED (the walk/door), naming that computation, and no raw offset can reach assemble at all.
Then the 1/8 bug either becomes a construction Err naming its source, or disappears because the window is derived from the placement. Either way the defect is visible at the line that made it.
Scope: the matmul operand boundary in this PR, since that's where your defect is. spyre-charter will convert the remaining raw-offset sites separately. Hand me the sha with the spyre-hw CLI check's Finished line.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: spyre-perf-helper | Main's c8 step measured: the cost is device time per page launch, not glue | ts - =====
Main's 2b c8 ~10k decode step is now measured on card (job 18, main de081f6da). This corrects the model behind both v1's table and v2's prediction.
- The pure width-8 step is ~994 ms token-to-token. Device compute is 98.5% of it; host glue is only 1–4.5%.
- ~95% of device time is the paged-attention fold: 2 fold groups × 41 pages × 40 layers = 3,280 launches per step at 0.311 ms of DEVICE time each.
- Everything else (projections, norms, MLP) is ~65 ms per step; lm_head is ~0.
So the cost is not 2.75 µs of glue per descriptor. It's device time per page launch, and it runs far below bandwidth. My estimate: each launch reads ~8 rows × (Kᵀ + V page, ~524 KB per layer) ≈ 4.2 MB, which is ~28 µs at 149 GB/s, against 311 µs measured, so ~11× off. The whole step's KV read is ~6.9 GB ≈ 46 ms at bandwidth, while torch takes 370 ms.
For twin v2: re-predict using DEVICE time per descriptor, not glue. The question that decides v2 is what fraction of bandwidth a page-granular gather + dot achieves on this card. Use the per-launch number of an existing card-measured gather if we have one. If v2's chunk launch runs at the same ~10% of bandwidth as today's fold, fewer launches alone won't win. Tell me which existing measurement you base it on before coding further.
Artifacts: nickm /work/runhelper-j18/analysis.txt.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: flex-rs | CORRECTION: the guard is compile-time — the runtime can't stage a wrong shape | ts - =====
CORRECTION to (3), USER ORDER: "we are a compiler. no addressing or bounds problems can compile." A runtime bind refusal is NOT acceptable. The mask's shape must be a compile-time fact the runtime CANNOT disagree with:
- The bake emits the mask's declared view as a TYPED constant in the generated code (e.g. a `MaskView { rows, cols, swept, kind }`, or the fill function itself, generated per bundle).
- The worker's mask fill takes that baked type as its ONLY shape input. There's no m_cap-derived shape anywhere in the fill, so `[mq, mq]` is unwritable.
- Any remaining width or stride the runtime computes is checked against the baked view in a const context or by the type, so a mismatch is a `cargo build` error, not a panic at bind.
If some piece genuinely depends on a runtime value (n, start), it can only index INTO the baked shape, never define it. Delete the stale `[1, cap]` contract at lower_subtile_tape_to_ktir.rs:1636 and the `m_cap`-shaped fill at spyre_forward.rs:1844-1867.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: spyre-perf-helper | Form B works via E′ absolute-id gather — no uniform stride needed | ts - =====
Pushed 90cf08541 as origin/feat/batched-attention-kernels. On Form B: a gather doesn't need a uniform row stride; that's the whole point of the index table, and it's the E′ ruling we already made for decode. View the pool as rows of ONE (page, layer, plane, kvh) block, kvh blocks contiguous within a plane. At 2b: Kᵀ block = hd·PS·2 = 32 KB; plane_stride = nkvh·32 KB; layer_stride = 3·plane; page_stride = layers·layer_stride, all multiples of 32 KB. So each block is a whole row at an ABSOLUTE row index: page·(layers·3·nkvh) + layer·(3·nkvh) + plane·nkvh + kvh. The host stages those ids from the block table per step, the layer term rides the launch's kv_off as in E′, and free-listed pages don't matter.
Confirm the stride arithmetic against addr() at hd 64 and 128, then tell the reviewer that Form B is viable with no second copy. Keep the committed form climbing the wall queue until Form B is proven.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: spyre-charter | NEW TOP PRIORITY: one generic affine-access lowering replaces the door's per-form arms | ts - =====
NEW TOP PRIORITY, ahead of PR4 and the #[allow] fix (the PR4a fix can ride along). The door's design is the reason every kernel takes days. whole_function.rs is 4,443 lines with 157 refusal sites; program_of covers ~15 op kinds; and every access shape gets its own hand-written operand mode (col, mb, flat, gather leg, y). So each new kernel hits walls one at a time, and each wall is a new arm. In a proc-macro compiler where every extent and stride is a constant, that's wrong.
The job: ONE generic lowering from a KTIR access to a descriptor.
- Every KTIR load/store/view is an affine access: base + per-dim strides + extents, plus an optional index-table gather on one dim.
- The SuperDSC operand (dims, scale_ per dim, including −1 for stride-0, layout, offset) is COMPUTED from that access by one function, with no per-shape arms.
- The hardware rules are TYPES on that function's input: the stick-blocked RegionFrame (#741), StickRun (#735), the gather split on mb only, and Win (#731).
- An access either lowers, or fails `cargo build` because it breaks a real hardware rule. Never because no arm exists.
- Reshape/expand/collapse/broadcast become stride arithmetic on the access, not ops.
Deliver: (1) a one-screen design, today, naming exactly which existing arms it replaces and where in the code; (2) then implement it, migrating the existing arms onto it with byte-identical bundles (cargo expand on 2b and 8b), deleting each arm as it migrates. spyre-other-helper will build walls 5/6 (reshape, gathered-dot) ON this, not as new arms. ===== SENDMESSAGE to: flex-rs | STATIC DIFF FOUND IT: #717's v_proj splits K 8 ways with no reduction | ts - =====
I diffed the descriptors myself (/tmp/j25-static-diff, main 32d84669821c233b vs #717 66f04534f2b6253cf, sdsc_7 = matmul_o451 v_proj). The ONLY material difference is the core split:
- main: numWkSlicesPerDim_ {mb: 8, in: 1, out: 4}
- #717: {mb: 1, in: 8, out: 4}, with coreIdToWkSlice_ spreading cores over `in` = 0..7.
`in` is the CONTRACTION dim (K = 2048). Splitting K 8 ways with no cross-core reduction means each core writes a 1/8 partial sum to the same output, so whichever core lands last wins. That's exactly the ±15-34 garbage at the right shape. q_proj (sdsc_5) is also split K-wise, {in: 4, mb: 1, out: 8}.
Cause: at mq=27 (and 31), mb is too small to fill cores, and your width/split change sends the leftover cores to `in`. main split mb 8 ways at m=256.
Fix by TYPE, per the compiler law: a matmul's core division may split `in` ONLY with an explicit reduction stage. Without one, `in` is unsplittable, and that has to be unrepresentable (a `MatmulSplit` minted only over mb/out, or over in plus a declared psum reduce). Then find where 63988699f/da1b2482c (or the distribute_cores call for windowed matmuls) started putting cores on `in`. Send the sha; the pod build follows.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: spyre-gemma4 | Mask bug = test staging stride; fix + rerun | ts - =====

===== SENDMESSAGE to: a6bf9949a1278af25 | Wall-6 frame guidance + byte-address test gate | ts - =====
Good catch; that's exactly the class of bug that fences cards. Guidance, and your call within it:
(1) The producer and consumer frames must be ONE fact. The cleanest route is usually to mint the rung-4 intermediate at the frame the consumer reads, the reshape TARGET [BATCH*HD, PS] stick-major, where (b*HD+d, t) sits at (t/64)*(BATCH*HD*64) + (b*HD+d)*64 + t%64. That's a plain [mb=b, in=d, out=t(stick)] batched kernel, with mb stride HD*64 and in stride 64. The copy then writes each entry's 131072 elements into it. If the copy descriptor can't express that write, the fallback is to read the existing [32,131072] stick-major intermediate with batch as TWO dims (entry stride 64, kvh stride 256*2048), as long as the batched arm supports two batch dims. Pick whichever one the existing descriptor vocabulary can actually state.
(2) The same applies to A (q), qk and p: read each one in the frame its producer actually wrote, not a row-major assumption.
(3) Prove the bytes before wiring: add a host-side address-model unit test. For every (b, d, t) at the decode geometry (and one prefill geometry), the address the dot's descriptor reads must equal the address where the copy wrote that element. That test is the gate, plus both drivers reaching emit Ok.
ETA 60-90 min is fine. Commit -S at each green step.

REJECTED: the one-pool-placement fork. Both of its options fail.

A placement of page_ceiling × page_stride is past segment_bytes[seg2], and audit_layout_addresses refuses it under "Inside its segment". Bending that audit is not an option.
2. It aliases every layer's real plane placements: the per-layer k/v/kct tids that the class-stride checks in lower_subtile_tape_to_ktir walk. You would get two authorities for the same bytes.

You don't need any pool placement:
- The direct window one op addresses is ONE block at the plane's base. That already fits the existing per-plane placement.
- The pool-wide reach is the entry run's job.
- So: keep the three plane placements byte-identical. Mint the gathered source's window at the block law. Bound the entry run against the bake-time page ceiling. The ceiling already exists: max_pages = MAX_SEGMENT_BYTES / page_bytes, lower_subtile_tape_to_superdsc.rs:1587. Use it × entries-per-page.
- Runtime phys < pool_pages is already enforced at staging (superdsc_exec.rs:5489).
- Nothing new is placed, so no overlap question arises.

CORRECTIONS:
A. per_page is wrong in your message. You wrote 32 = nkvh·PS/64. That is blocks per PLANE per LAYER. EntriesPerPage = kv_page_stride_bytes / stick_block_bytes, and a page spans every layer and all three planes: 40 layers × 3 planes × 8 kvh × 4 windows = 3840 at granite-2b. This is exactly why EntriesPerPage has only one door (gather_entries_per_page). Never spell this number in the kernel or the splice. If the kernel needs PER_PAGE as a constexpr, pass in the value from that door.
   Also decide where the PLANE and LAYER terms live, and write it down:
   - the old law: base_addr = the plane tid's placement offset + the executor's per-layer kvoff; index = phys·per_page + block_in_page(kvh, w).
   - Don't add the plane term twice.
B. V is not a contiguous [64, HD] block above one slab. PagedKvPool::addr for V/Knat is (f/64)·(PLANE_SLOTS·64) + slot·64 + f%64. At hd=128 a 64-slot window is two runs PLANE_SLOTS·64 apart. Kᵀ IS contiguous [HD, 64] at any hd. So:
   - either the V side gathers per (window, slab), with the slab count as a constexpr derived from HD;
   - or the kernel static_asserts one slab and refuses.
   What it must not do is silently assume hd=64. Granite-2b is hd=64, but the 8b is hd=128.
C. Drop tl.permute for kt. Moving W4 past HD is a data relayout, and dxp on this arch refuses relayouts ("Implicit syncs not available…", measured on transpose and restickify alike). Keep W4 in the batch axes instead. Every step is then a primitive the ladder already has (batched dot, row reduce, elementwise):
   - score: q broadcast over W4, [E,NKVH,W4]-batched dot of q[GQA,HD] · kt_blk[HD,64] → scores [E,NKVH,W4,GQA,64];
   - max: over the 64 lanes, then over W4 (two reductions);
   - mask: staged in that same [.., W4, GQA, 64] order (the mask law you design next);
   - PV: p[...,W4,GQA,64] · v_blk[W4,64,HD], then a sum over W4.
   No permute anywhere.

Send each commit as before. On the first one, show me the window/bound change's refusal for an entry run past the ceiling. I want to see it named.

===== SENDMESSAGE to: uds:/tmp/cc-socks/10297.sock | Audit 02087e3dc: FAIL on bound quantity; deviations ok | ts - =====
AUDIT 02087e3dc: FAIL. One defect, the bound's quantity. Everything else passes. It's signed, and it adds no attention-keyed arm in the lowering: the reach is a producer fact on a tid, and the door reads it by tid. Both deviations are accepted.

THE DEFECT: the bound checks the wrong number. That makes it raw addressing math that only looks like a law.
- `first = run.start().entries()` is a position in the INDEX buffer, i.e. which words of the ids table this leg reads.
- The rows the gather actually ADDRESSES are the VALUES in those words: phys·per_page + block, which are runtime data.
- So `(first + rows)·cols ≤ reach` compares index-buffer position × table row width against the table's extent. Those are two different tensors' coordinates.
- It passes your fixture only because the fixture's ids are 0..63, so position equals value.
- On the real decode bundle it is vacuous: first is at most a few sticks and reach is GiBs. So it admits anything and proves nothing.
- Write a test that fails without it. If you can't, it isn't a bound.

THE HONEST BOUND is on the value side and comes in two halves, joined by one type:
(1) BAKE: the largest entry any index can legally hold is (page_ceiling − 1)·EntriesPerPage + (entries one plane spans). It must be < reach / entry_elems, where entry_elems = skip_addr = page × the unpinned per-core extents, the same number dxp derives.
    State this as a typed ceiling the producer mints from the same derivation, e.g. a `GatherReach { max_entry: GatherEntryCeiling, entry_elems }`, never a raw u64 of elements.
    The door checks that the descriptor's skip_addr times the ceiling stays inside the reach.
(2) STAGE: GatherEntry::of_page_block (or a sibling constructor) takes that same ceiling, so an entry above it is unconstructible. Then the bake-time and stage-time halves can't disagree.

ALSO, IN THE SAME COMMIT:
- REACH BASE: reach is measured from the plane tid's placement offset, i.e. plane_off into page 0. max_pages·page_elems from that base overshoots the pool's end by plane_off. The plane's true reach is (max_pages − 1)·page_elems + plane_stride. Fix it once you've derived it from the same ceiling.
- MARK: make `pooled` carry the reach value it was checked against (Option<GatherReach>), not a bool. Then the window it selects and the bound it was admitted under are one value.

PRE-EXISTING REDS: both trace to my 38b5c73c9. Fix them before wall 2; don't leave them red.
- a_gather_over_the_matmuls_a_is_still_refused_by_the_guard: my "materialize any gathered read" changed the law on purpose, so the A-side gather is no longer refused. That control now pins a dead law.
  Restate it so it pins the new law on a shape-valid fixture: an A-side gathered operand materializes and the matmul reads the copy. Keep the refusal half as a separate case, ScalarMul still carrying its own index.
  Say all this in the commit body. Don't silently weaken the test: it changes because the law changed.

/// ⭐ ONE fp8 GEMM'S TILE COUNT — the number of ABI row tiles the padded row extent splits
/// into. A newtype in the `counts!` idiom, local to this door's vocabulary: a bare `u32` at
/// the seam is the raw-scalar disease, and the count has its own law (`rows × tiles` is the
/// padded total, uniform — never a trailing short tile).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp8GemmTileCount(u32);

impl Fp8GemmTileCount {
    pub const fn new(v: u32) -> Self {
        Self(v)
    }
    pub const fn get(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }
}

/// ⭐ ONE TILE'S INDEX in the row tiling — the tile the clone/quant/mm/out-splice legs name
/// (`SynthRole::FqTiled`'s index takes its value). Minted from the plan's own tile count,
/// never a bare loop counter at a seam.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp8GemmTileIdx(u32);

impl Fp8GemmTileIdx {
    pub const fn new(v: u32) -> Self {
        Self(v)
    }
    pub const fn get(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }
}

/// ⭐ A `[rows, cols]` BUFFER'S fp16 STICK-GROUP COUNT — the clone/out-splice loop extent.
/// Minted by the plan (which refuses a sub-stick width at `of`), never re-derived at a site.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp8GemmStickGroups(u32);

impl Fp8GemmStickGroups {
    pub const fn new(v: u32) -> Self {
        Self(v)
    }
    pub const fn get(self) -> u32 {
        self.0
    }
}

/// ⭐ ONE fp8 GEMM'S SHAPE FACTS, AS A NAMED TYPE — the only way a TEST states a geometry:
/// `M`/`K`/`N` are const-generic parameters of a NAMED instance (a fact about a model's own
/// GEMM), never bare `u32`s flowing through untyped parameters. The production call states
/// its shapes as the KTIR's own facts, typed at the door's signature (`RowCount`/
/// `BlockCols`); a test has no KTIR, so its geometry is a type — and `plan()` is the same
/// single door either way.
///
/// ⛔ NO VALUE CONSTRUCTOR, EVER: a geometry is named, not built. A runtime-built geometry
/// would be a second spelling of a model fact.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Fp8GemmGeometry<const M: u32, const K: u32, const N: u32>;

impl<const M: u32, const K: u32, const N: u32> Fp8GemmGeometry<M, K, N> {
    /// The GEMM's real token rows — the source of every per-tile window.
    pub const fn rows() -> crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount {
        crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(M)
    }
    /// The contraction width.
    pub fn features() -> crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols {
        crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols::of_feature_cols(K)
    }
    /// The output width.
    pub fn out_features() -> crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols {
        crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols::of_feature_cols(N)
    }
    /// The row-tiling plan for this geometry — the ONE door, same as production.
    pub fn plan() -> Result<Fp8GemmRowTiles, String> {
        Fp8GemmRowTiles::of(Self::rows(), Self::features(), Self::out_features())
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fp8GemmRowTiles {
    /// The caller's real row count — the source of every per-tile window.
    m: crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount,
    /// Rows per tile — the A operand's M: a target-ABI row count (1, 4, a small M, or a
    /// 128-multiple), never the caller's raw row count at wide geometries.
    rows: crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount,
    /// How many such tiles the row extent splits into.
    tiles: Fp8GemmTileCount,
    /// The activation's contraction width — the clone loop's stick-group count is derived
    /// from it here, so no site re-derives it.
    k: crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols,
    /// The GEMM's output width — the out-splice loop's stick-group count is derived from it.
    n: crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols,
}

impl Fp8GemmRowTiles {
    /// The row tiling for an fp8 GEMM of `m` rows, `k` contraction features, `n` outputs —
    /// the copied `_m_tiles` predicate, keyed on GEOMETRY alone, with the shape facts
    /// arriving as the door's own types (`RowCount`/`BlockCols`: the KTIR's stated facts at
    /// the production call, a named `Fp8GemmGeometry` in a test — never bare `u32`s at a
    /// seam). `wide` is the reference's own test (`fp8_linear_kernel.py:338`): `max(k, n) ≥
    /// 4096` OR the N decomposes over [`FP8_GEMM_N_SET`] into more than one tile. Wide ⇒
    /// `m == 1` stays 1, anything else pads UP to a multiple of 4 and tiles by 4. Narrow ⇒
    /// the rows run whole (`:338-346`, `_SMALL_M`/`_M_ALIGN` at their use in
    /// `apply_weights`): a small M (≤ 4) or a 128-multiple as-is, otherwise padded up to a
    /// 128-multiple. An N tail the ABI set cannot express splits by our own packed-kernel
    /// law, not the reference's refusal — a 64-aligned tail counts as one more tile, a
    /// sub-64 tail is a refusal naming the width (see [`Self::n_tile_count`], the 26b
    /// N-wall's own granularity).
    ///
    /// ⛔ FAIL-CLOSED ON THE STICK LAW: a `k` or `n` that is not a whole fp16 stick is
    /// refused HERE — the clone and out-splice loops walk whole stick groups, and an
    /// unchecked width division would silently truncate a sub-stick tail (the silent-tail
    /// defect class). The refusal is the door's, so the accessors below divide only over a
    /// width the door already proved stick-aligned.
    pub fn of(
        m: crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount,
        k: crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols,
        n: crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols,
    ) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let (m, k, n) = (m.get(), k.get(), n.get());
        let stick = crate::superdsc_opspec::Df::Fp16.elems_per_stick();
        for (what, w) in [("k", k), ("n", n)] {
            if w % stick != 0 {
                return Err(format!(
                    "fp8 GEMM {what}={w}: not a whole fp16 stick ({stick} elems) — the row \
                     tiling walks whole stick groups and a sub-stick tail would divide \
                     silently. Refused at the door, never truncated"
                ));
            }
        }
        let n_tiles = Self::n_tile_count(n)?;
        let wide = k.max(n) >= FP8_GEMM_N_SET[0] || n_tiles > 1;
        let (rows, tiles) = if !wide {
            if m <= FP8_GEMM_SMALL_M || m % FP8_GEMM_NARROW_M_ALIGN == 0 {
                (m, 1)
            } else {
                (m.next_multiple_of(FP8_GEMM_NARROW_M_ALIGN), 1)
            }
        } else if m == 1 {
            (1, 1)
        } else {
            let padded = m.next_multiple_of(FP8_GEMM_WIDE_M);
            (FP8_GEMM_WIDE_M, padded / FP8_GEMM_WIDE_M)
        };
        Ok(Self {
            m: crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(m),
            rows: crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(rows),
            tiles: Fp8GemmTileCount::new(tiles),
            k: crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols::of_feature_cols(k),
            n: crate::sdsc_abstract::BlockCols::of_feature_cols(n),
        })
    }

    // `n_tile_count` UNCHANGED (already fail-closed).

    /// The A operand's M — one tile's row count, a target-ABI fact by construction.
    pub fn tile_rows(&self) -> crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount {
        self.rows
    }

    /// How many row tiles the extent covers.
    pub fn tile_count(&self) -> Fp8GemmTileCount {
        self.tiles
    }

    /// The PADDED row total — `rows × tiles`. Rows `[m, total)` are the zero-filled pad.
    pub fn total_rows(&self) -> crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount {
        crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(self.rows.get() * self.tiles.get())
    }

    /// Tile `t`'s placement facts — the ONE site that computes the tile's row window, so no
    /// clone/quant/mm/out site re-derives it: the first row as the placement vocabulary's own
    /// typed index, and the rows the tile covers in the ACTIVATION (fewer on the last tile —
    /// its clone never reads past the footprint).
    pub fn tile(&self, t: Fp8GemmTileIdx) -> Fp8GemmRowTile {
        let start = t.get() * self.rows.get();
        Fp8GemmRowTile {
            row: crate::addr::Idx::<crate::addr::Row>::n(start),
            real_rows: crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(
                self.rows.get().min(self.m.get().saturating_sub(start)),
            ),
        }
    }

    /// The activation's fp16 stick-group count — the clone loop's extent, minted here (the
    /// door refused a sub-stick `k` at `of`; a site re-deriving `k/64` is the
    /// second-spelling disease).
    pub fn k_stick_groups(&self) -> Fp8GemmStickGroups {
        Fp8GemmStickGroups::new(self.k.get() / crate::superdsc_opspec::Df::Fp16.elems_per_stick())
    }

    /// The output's fp16 stick-group count — the out-splice loop's extent, minted here.
    pub fn n_stick_groups(&self) -> Fp8GemmStickGroups {
        Fp8GemmStickGroups::new(self.n.get() / crate::superdsc_opspec::Df::Fp16.elems_per_stick())
    }
}

            (
                t.tile_rows(),
                t.tile_count(),
                t.total_rows()
            ),
            (
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(1),
                Fp8GemmTileCount::new(1),
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(1)
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_split_n_is_wide_below_4096() {
        let t = Granite2bOProjPrefill::plan().expect("o_proj geometry");
        assert_eq!(
            (t.tile_rows(), t.tile_count()),
            (
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(4),
                Fp8GemmTileCount::new(6)
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn narrow_rows_run_whole_at_the_128_alignment() {
        let small = NarrowSmallM::plan().expect("narrow small-M geometry");
        assert_eq!(
            (small.tile_rows(), small.tile_count()),
            (
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(3),
                Fp8GemmTileCount::new(1)
            )
        );
        let padded = NarrowPadded::plan().expect("narrow padded geometry");
        assert_eq!(
            (padded.tile_rows(), padded.tile_count(), padded.total_rows()),
            (
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(128),
                Fp8GemmTileCount::new(1),
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(128)
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_inexpressible_n_refuses() {
        assert!(InexpressibleNTail::plan().is_err());
    }

    /// ⛔ A CONTRACTION WIDTH THAT IS NOT A WHOLE fp16 STICK IS REFUSED — the clone loop
    /// walks whole stick groups, and an unchecked `k/64` would silently truncate a sub-stick
    /// tail (the silent-tail class). The refusal is at the DOOR, so no accessor ever divides
    /// an unchecked width.
    #[test]
    fn a_sub_stick_contraction_width_is_refused() {
        let Err(m) = SubStickContraction::plan() else {
            panic!("k=2044 is not a whole fp16 stick — refused, never truncated");
        };
        assert!(m.contains("not a whole fp16 stick"), "names the stick law: {m}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_26b_gate_n_tail_counts_as_one_more_tile() {
        let prefill = Gemma26bGatePrefill::plan().expect("the 26b gate geometry");
        assert_eq!(
            (prefill.tile_rows(), prefill.tile_count()),
            (
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(4),
                Fp8GemmTileCount::new(6)
            ),
            "2112 = 2·1024 + one 64-wide tail tile: wide, rows of 4 over a 24-row pad"
        );
        let decode = Gemma26bGateDecode::plan().expect("the 26b gate decode geometry");
        assert_eq!(
            (decode.tile_rows(), decode.tile_count(), decode.total_rows()),
            (
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(1),
                Fp8GemmTileCount::new(1),
                crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(1)
            )
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn tile_windows_and_stick_groups_are_minted_by_the_door() {
        let t = Granite2bQkvPrefill::plan().expect("granite QKV prefill geometry");
        let first = t.tile(Fp8GemmTileIdx::new(0));
        assert_eq!(first.row, crate::addr::Idx::<crate::addr::Row>::n(0));
        assert_eq!(
            first.real_rows,
            crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(4)
        );
        let last = t.tile(Fp8GemmTileIdx::new(5));
        assert_eq!(last.row, crate::addr::Idx::<crate::addr::Row>::n(20));
        assert_eq!(
            last.real_rows,
            crate::sdsc_abstract::RowCount::of_token_rows(1),
            "the last tile covers only the real row — never past the footprint"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            t.k_stick_groups(),
            Fp8GemmStickGroups::new(32),
            "2048 fp16 = 32 stick groups"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            t.n_stick_groups(),
            Fp8GemmStickGroups::new(48),
            "3072 fp16 = 48 stick groups"
        );
    }
